start_walkthrough.title: Start walkthrough
start_walkthrough.description: Create a narrated walkthrough. Call it first, before reading files or researching: the opening plays while you do. Pass its opening in `opening`: the reply then comes once that is voiced, with the handle, the playable link and the full authoring guide. Send the link to the user at once, in a message, before your next tool call; they watch while you add the body with add_slides. Without `opening`, the reply is short and your first add_slides call must carry the opening instead.

args.title: Walkthrough title, shown on the title slide and in the player. Lead with the subject's keywords; under about 50 characters fits the title slide.
args.description: One or two sentences on what the walkthrough covers and for whom, up to 200 characters. Shown in the list and gallery and written into exported files as metadata; never spoken or shown on a slide.
args.frame: Slide shape: landscape (default, 1280×720), square (960×960) or portrait (720×1280, for phones).
args.voice: English Kokoro voice id, or a description such as `British male` or `American female, soft` for the closest one. Omit for the default. Voices:
args.speed: Speech rate from 0.8 to 1.3; 1.0 is normal.
args.project_dir: Absolute path of the project. Code blocks with file= and image paths are read from it and must stay inside it. Defaults to the client's root, then the server's working directory.
args.opening:
The opening in Markdown, voiced before this call returns: a `#` title heading, an optional `>` subtitle line, then one or two short spoken sentences as a plain paragraph that hold without research: the question, the goal or why it matters, and any fact the request gives; what you have yet to read waits for later slides. Nothing more; the body goes in add_slides. Example:
# How the retry loop works
> Backoff in the HTTP client

A failed request can be sent up to four times. We'll follow one through the client.
args.theme: Colour theme: dark (default), light, paper (warm light), night (indigo and pink), ocean (teal and coral), studio (bright, violet) or contrast (high contrast). Pick one that suits the subject. Omit to use the project's showntell.theme.json or the default. Viewers can switch it.

add_slides.title: Add slides
add_slides.description:
Append slides to a walkthrough, written in Markdown.

Calls:
- Opening: normally sent in start_walkthrough's `opening` (see its example). Only if it was not sent there, the first call carries it and nothing more: the title slide and one or two short spoken sentences. That call returns when the link is playable, with the full guide; send the link to the user then, before anything else.
- All other calls: first one short slide alone, then one to three whole slides. Never resend earlier Markdown. Never split a slide or its code block across calls.
- Replies list problems, each ending in a code; errors come first. Fix errors in sent slides now with revise_slide; fix warnings in later slides.

Format:
- Slide: each #, ## or ### heading starts one. Optional attributes: `## Title {#id .build}`; .build reveals parts as cues reach them.
- Narration: every plain paragraph is spoken, labels included, each voiced separately: never start one with "Narration:" or "Slide 3:". Put identifiers in `backticks`; `[text]{say="spoken"}` fixes pronunciation.
- Shown text: `>` lines are shown, never spoken; under the first heading, one is the subtitle.
- Layout: `>` under a heading is its takeaway; {.side} puts one to three `>` lines beside the visual, {.pair} shows two visuals side by side, {.full} the visual edge to edge; a slide with only a `>` sentence is a statement. {icon=name} on a heading, and `:name:` before a list item, stat label or `>` line, add a Lucide icon. Vary the look from slide to slide.
- Visual: at most one per slide: fenced code, diff, ```mermaid diagram, ```math formula, pipe table, list, image ![alt](path), ```chart bar|hbar|line, ```terminal session, ```tree of files, ```stat numbers, ```chat exchange, ```svg drawing (consecutive ```svg step blocks are versions that glide into each other; ```svg sketch looks hand-drawn) or ```drawio file=path, a draw.io diagram the project already has. Syntax and examples: resource showntell://slide-kinds.
- Choose the visual by the idea's shape: a change → diff, not the new code alone; flow, steps, causes and effects → ```mermaid; numbers → chart or stat; something physical or spatial → ```svg drawing; commands → ```terminal; dated events → .timeline list. Lists and tables only for words with no shape, never three in a row.
- Code options: `scroll` for long code; consecutive ```lang step blocks are versions of one code slide.
- Code from disk, with an empty body and the file's own line numbers in the gutter:
```python file=src/app.py lines=10-24
```
  Inline code may set start=10.
- Diff: ```python old then ```python new blocks; ```diff with -/+ lines, one hunk per slide; or ```diff file=path rev=A (against the working tree), rev=A..B (two commits) or rev=A...B (B against the commit where it branched off A: what a pull request shows).
- List: `- **Title**: text {#id}`; without {#id}, the id is the title, lowercased and hyphenated. `1.` items are steps; .cards on the heading shows cards; .timeline puts dates, the bold titles, on a line; .quiz makes two to four `- [ ]` items with one `- [x]` a multiple-choice question, choices #a to #d, the answer shown when a cue points at it.
- Cues are links in narration around the words that name the target. The pointer lands as the label's first word is spoken, within the current slide only.
  [label](#L12) line 12 | #L12-18 a range | [label](#L12 "exact text") only that text on line 12 | #-L5 old side, #+L7 new side of a diff | #id a list item, card, Mermaid node, chart bar or series, tree entry, drawing element (also by its <title> or text as a slug) or draw.io cell (also by a unique label) | #row-2 the second table row, or a {#id} ending its last cell | # the whole visual; [label](# "text") finds that text in it. Also #step-2 (only with step blocks), #a->b->c flowchart edge path, #Sender->>Receiver a sequence-diagram message, #@l,t,w,h image, drawing or draw.io region; {.circle}, {.arrow}, {.zoom} etc. after a cue (see showntell://slide-kinds).

args.markdown: Slides in Markdown: one to three whole slides, nothing already sent. Only when the opening was not sent with start_walkthrough: the first call carries just the title slide and one or two spoken sentences.

revise_slide.title: Revise slide
revise_slide.description: Replace one slide, found by its id, with new Markdown. Only narration whose text changed is voiced again; the rest keeps its audio. Omit the heading to keep the slide's title, classes and attributes. Use it for a slide a reply reported as broken, or to rework a finished walkthrough: find its handle with list_walkthroughs and read its Markdown from the resource showntell://walkthroughs/{id}. The reply's slide_url plays only the revised slide; share it when the user asked for the change.

args.slide: Id of the slide to replace: its {#id}, or the id generated from its title as named in replies.
args.markdown: The complete new slide: heading (optional), visual, shown text and narration. One slide only.

finish_walkthrough.title: Finish walkthrough
finish_walkthrough.description: Close the walkthrough after its last slide. Records the end questions and returns a summary: remaining problems, each slide's start time and look (kind, layout, takeaway, icons) and what could not be checked. It names runs of slides that look alike, with pictures of them; revise one in each run into a different look before telling the user. Once its browser is ready (fetched in the background on first run) it first draws every slide, so the summary already reports render and layout problems (render errors, text_too_small, overflow, drawing_overlap); fix them with revise_slide. Call preview_slides only for slides it names, a drawing or diagram you want to see, or when the user asks. Then tell the user it is finished and give the link; if they want a video or a file to send, call export_walkthrough.

args.questions: Two or three short follow-up questions the viewer might ask next, as a list of strings. Offered at the end of the walkthrough. Optional when the Markdown already lists them under a `.questions` heading; questions passed here replace those.

export_walkthrough.title: Export walkthrough
export_walkthrough.description: Save a walkthrough as one file the user can keep or forward: an MP4 video (H.264 and AAC, with a subtitle track) or a self-contained HTML page that plays offline in a browser. Call it after finish_walkthrough and the fixes its reply names. It waits up to five minutes for narration still being voiced, then renders; an MP4 takes about a tenth of its length plus a few seconds. Use it when the user asks for a video, or for a file to share, send or attach. MP4 needs ffmpeg and showntell's browser, HTML neither; the error says what is missing or still downloading.

args.format: mp4 (default): a video for chat apps, email and phones. html: one page that plays offline in a browser.
args.path: Where to write. Empty: a file named after the title in the project folder. Relative: inside the project folder. Absolute: that path, inside a folder the client shares. Must end in .mp4 or .html to match `format`. An existing file is overwritten.
args.max_mb: Size limit in MB. An MP4 over it is shrunk, first lower audio bitrate, then 720p; if it still does not fit, the call fails: split the walkthrough or raise the limit. An HTML page over it fails. 0: no limit. Omit for the server default: 16 (WhatsApp's video limit) when the user receives files, otherwise none. Other channels: Telegram bots 50, Signal 100, email often 25.

list_walkthroughs.title: List walkthroughs
list_walkthroughs.description: List recent walkthroughs with their handles, titles and links. Use it to find the handle of a walkthrough to revise later, including one from an earlier session. Its Markdown source is the resource showntell://walkthroughs/{id}, where id is the part of the handle before the dot.

preview_slides.title: Preview slides
preview_slides.description: Look at slides as the viewer sees them: returns a small picture of each, fully revealed, plus any layout problems the player found while drawing them. Use it for chosen slides (one a reply named, a drawing or diagram, a revised slide) to check that code is readable, diagrams fit and nothing overlaps; finish_walkthrough already draws every slide and reports these problems, so a full preview after it is rarely needed. Needs Playwright on the machine running showntell; the reply says how to install it if missing.

args.slides: Slide ids to show. Omit for all slides, up to twelve; with more, the last twelve.
